data.name: Alexandro
data.gender_notes: Alexandro is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek, Alex- (helper) and andros (man). This name means 'defender of the people'. In the New Testament, Saint Alexander was a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity and defended the faith against persecution. The name Alexandro carries the meaning “Defender of the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alexandro usually hope their child will grow to embody defender of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A protector and defender of spiritual values and beliefs.
data.etymology: Alexandro belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Defender of the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alexandro total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: אלכסנדרו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלכסנדרו הוא שם שפירושו 'מגן האדם' או 'מגן האנושות', נגזר מהמילים היווניות 'אלכסein' שפירושו 'להגן' ו'אנδρός' שפירושו 'אדם'. השם אלכסנדרו הוא תרגום של השם היווני אלכסנדרוס (Αλέξανδρος), ששימש ככינויו של המלך אלכסנדר הגדול, כובש ומלך מפורסם בתקופה ההלניסטית. השם אלכסנדרו מופיע גם בכתבי הקודש הנוצרים ומשמש כשם נוצרי.

in_greek.name: Αλεξάνδρο
in_greek.meaning: Αλεξάνδρο - αλεξein ανδρός, προστατεύω τον άνθρωπο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αλεξάνδρο προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'αλεξein' που σημαίνει 'να προστατεύω' και 'ανδρός' που σημαίνει 'άνθρωπος'. Ο Αλέξανδρος ήταν ένας από τους πιο διάσημους ονομάτων στην αρχαιότητα, χάρη στον Μέγα Αλέξανδρο, τον βασιλιά και κατακτητή. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα Αλέξανδρος αναφέρεται σε διάφορους ανθρώπους, συμπεριλαμβανομένου ενός από τους γιους του βασιλιά Ηρώδη.

in_latin.name: Alexandro
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Alexandro derivatur ex verbis Graecis 'alexein' quod significat 'defendere' et 'andros' quod significat 'hominem'. Alexandro fuit nomen celeberrimum in antiquitate, propter Alexandrum Magnum, regem et victorem. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Alexandro usitatum erat inter christianos, qui virtutem et protectionem divina requirebant.

in_english.name: Alexandro
in_english.meaning: Defender of the people, protector of humanity
in_english.long_meaning: The name Alexandro originates from the Greek words 'alexein' meaning 'to defend' and 'andros' meaning 'man'. It is associated with Alexander the Great, a renowned king and conqueror in ancient times. In Christian tradition, Alexandro symbolizes strength, courage, and divine protection. The name has been used across various cultures and is still popular today, reflecting its timeless significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Alexander has been popular throughout history in various cultures, not just in its Greek origin. In the Middle Ages, it became a favorite among European royalty. Many famous rulers, including Alexander the Great, Tsar Alexander I of Russia, and King Alexander of Yugoslavia, bear this name. Additionally, the name has been used in literature and mythology, such as the character Alexandre Dumas in The Three Musketeers.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, Saint Alexander is revered as a protector and defender of the faith. He is the patron saint of the Roman military, blacksmiths, swordsmiths, and joiners. Alexander is said to have defended the faith against persecution and was subjected to numerous trials and tortures for his belief in Christianity. His bravery and unwavering faith in the face of adversity make him an inspiring figure for believers. The name Alexander carries a spiritual significance of courage, strength, and protecting and defending one's beliefs.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Alexandro: Greek origin meaning "defender of the people." This name symbolizes strength, courage, and protection. It is a reminder to be a shield for those in need and to stand firm in the face of adversity.
